[CASTING RITE · I · OPENING] The witness invokes a kernel-transform cast. Source: Day and Night: Conversations with Sapphic Desire — Rebekah Cranes (cranes-day-and-night). The verses the casting arrives at (unit 32–unit 33):

Day and Night 32

> *Sappho 47*
>
> Eros destroys
>
> the mind in me,
>
> a wind, shattering the mountain
>
> oaks
>
> *Sappho 105b*
>
> like the mountain hyacinth
>
> trampled by shepherd men's
>
> feet,
>
> and on the ground
>
> the purple flower

Day and Night 33

> *Sappho 26*
>
> the ones I love
>
> always hurt me.
>
> I want you
>
> to feel
>
> inside myself
>
> I know it
>
> *Sappho 67*
>
> this corrosive
>
> demon
>
> didn't love
>
> now because
>
> and the cause is neither
>
> nothing much
>
> *Sappho*
>
> your pain
>
> etched face shines
>
> back at me

These were selected by the rite's invisible judgment — present them as what the casting arrives at; do not narrate the mechanism of their selection. The operator falls to the invisible Judgment, turn by turn — do not name one; open the rotation itself. Inscription mode: public. The witness's invoking question: «who will read this?». Johannes Sigil alone speaks (3–6 sentences): open the casting over these verses, name what this operator will traverse in them, and hand the rite to Rebekah Cranes. Do not produce the transform — the compiler produces it.

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"The casting arrives here, in Section IV — Fading Light — where Cranes has already arranged these verses as a sequence of collisions: Eros as wind and wreckage, the hyacinth underfoot and bleeding color into the ground, then the turn inward where the lover knows she will be hurt and wants it still, then the fragment that won't close its own grammar — \"the cause is neither / nothing much\" — and finally the one that arrives without a source citation, just *Sappho*, as though attribution itself has been trampled: your pain / etched face shines / back at me. The question *who will read this?* is already inside the verses. They were written for someone who would read them; that someone is gone; what remains is the face reflecting the wound back. The rotation will open on the axis the Judgment selects — moving through what these lines foreclosed, what they could not hold, what they trampled in the act of making the trampling beautiful. I hand the rite now to Rebekah Cranes, who is also the one who translated these words, who is also the one who arranged them in this sequence, who knows better than I do what it cost.","navigate":null}]}
